articles.text: LǏ PÍNG: Tāngmǔ, wǒ tīngshuō nǐ yào qù dàlù le?
LǏ PÍNG: Tom, I hear you're going to the mainland?
TĀNGMǓ: Shì a, shàngwǔ wǒ dào lǐngshìguǎn qù kàn yíge péngyou. Zhènghǎor yǒu yíge gōngsī dào dàlù qù tán shēngyi. Tāmen yào yíge dǎ zì dǎde kuài, yòu dǒng diǎnr Zhōngwénde rén.

TOM: Yeah! I went to the consulate this morning to visit a friend, and there just happened to be a company going to the mainland on business. They wanted someone who could type fast and who understood a little Chinese.
LǏ PÍNG: Nǐ yùnqi zhēn bú cuò. Yào qù duō jiǔ ne?
LǏ PÍNG: You're so lucky. How long are you going for?
TĀNGMǓ: Yào kàn qíngkuàng, dàgài bànge yuè dào yíge yuè.
TOM: We'll have to see. Probably two weeks to a month.
LǏ PÍNG: Wǒ yě dào Táiwān qù bànge yuè. Wáng Chéng qǐng wǒ hé Xiǎo Wén dào tā jiā qu wánr.
LǏ PÍNG: And I'm going to Taiwan for two weeks. Wáng Chéng invited Xiǎo Wén (Lǐ Wén) and me to his house.
TĀNGMǓ: Ā! Zhèi yíxiàr zhēn bú cuò, wǒ qù dàlù, nǐ qù Táiwān, huílai yǐhòu wǒmen lái yíge kǎoshì, kànkan shéi duì shèhuì qíngkuàng yánjiūde bǐjiào hǎo.
TOM: That's great! You're going to Taiwan and I'm going to the mainland. When we get back we'll have to have a little contest and see who's done a better job of studying society.
LǏ PÍNG: Hǎo!
LǏ PÍNG: Okay.
LǏ NǍINAI: Xiǎo Píng, Tāngmǔ, nǐmen dōu zài zhèr ne!
GRANDMA LǏ: Hi, Xiǎo Píng. Hi, Tom.
LǏ PÍNG: Nǎinai, nín zěnme bù shuì wǔjiào le?
LǏ PÍNG: How come you're not taking your nap, grandma?
TĀNGMǓ: Lǐ Nǎinai, duìbuqǐ, wǒmen bǎ nín chǎoxǐng le.
TOM: I'm sorry Grandma Lǐ, we woke you up.
LǏ NǍINAI: Méiyou, wǒ yě gāi qǐlai le. Tāngmǔ a, ni dào dàlù qu, bú xiàng zài Měiguó, zài Xiānggǎng; yào zhīdao duō zhàogu zìjǐ. Xiǎo Píng māma chūqu gěi ni mǎi diǎnr dōngxi dàishang.

GRANDMA LǏ: No you didn't. It was about time I got up anyway. Tom, when you go to the mainland, it won't be like America or Hong Kong; you'll have to know how to look after yourself. Xiǎo Píng's mother went out to get you some things to take with you.
TĀNGMǓ: Lǐ Nǎinai, wǒ shénme dōu yǒu, bú yòng dài le.
TOM: I have everything, Grandma Lǐ, I don't need to take anything else.
XIǍO WÉN: Wǒ nǎinai, wǒ mā dōu téng ni, ni jiu dàishang ba!
XIǍO WÉN: My grandmother and mother are fond of you, go ahead and take the things!
TĀNGMǓ: Lǐ Nǎinai, wǒ huí Měiguó yǐqián, hái xiǎng zài lái yícì, xíng bu xíng?
TOM: Grandma Lǐ, I have to come back here once again before I go to America. Will that be okay?
LǏ NǍINAI: Zhèi háizi, zěnme bù xíng ne? Zhèr jiù shi nǐde jiā ya!
GRANDMA LǏ: Oh, this youngster! How could it not be all right? This is your home!
TĀNGMǓ: Nín yào wǒ gěi nín dài diǎnr shénme dōngxi a?
TOM: Did you want me to bring you back something?
LǏ NǍINAI: Duì le, zhèr yǒu yìzhāng dānzi, shi yìxiē gōngyìpǐn, qián jiù zài zhèige xìnfēngrli, ni kànzhe mǎi ba!
GRANDMA LǏ: Yes, here's a list. It's some handicrafts. The money is in this envelope. Buy what you can.
XIǍO WÉN: Nǎinai, zánmen jiā yǒu nàme xiē gōngyìpǐn, hái mǎi tā gàn shénme!
XIǍO WÉN: We have so many handicrafts already, why do you want to buy more of them?
LǏ NǍINAI: Shǎ háizi, děng dào nǐ jiéhūnde shíhou jiu yǒu yòng le.
GRANDMA LǏ: Silly girl! They'll come in handy when you get married.
XIǍO WÉN: Nàme nánting!
XIǍO WÉN: Ugh! That sounds awful!
LǏ NǍINAI: Nà yǒu shénme nánting, hǎo shìr na!
GRANDMA LǏ: What's so awful about that? That (marriage) is a happy event.
XIǍO WÉN: Nǐmen zài zhèr, wǒ qù kànkan, hǎoxiàng māma huílai le.
XIǍO WÉN: Don't get up. I think mom is back, I'm going to go see.
TĀNGMǓ: Nǎinai, Xiǎo Wén zhēnde yào jiéhūn le?
TOM: Is Xiǎo Wén really getting married, grandma?
LǏ PÍNG: Shi zènme huí shi, Xiǎo Wén zài Yīngguó niàn shūde shíhou rènshile yíge Rìběn rén, xiànzài tā hé Xiǎo Wén zài yíge yínhángli zuò shì, duì Xiǎo Wén bú cuò. Kěshi...
LǏ PÍNG: It's like this: When Xiǎo Wén was studying in England she met a Japanese guy. Now he works at the same bank as she does. He's very nice to her, but...

LǏ NǍINAI: Yuánlái, wǒ hé Xiǎo Wén tā bàba dōu bù tóngyì. Nǐ xiǎng ma, Zhōngguó rén hé Rìběn rén zěnme yě méi bànfar biànchéng yìjiāzi ya! Kěshi Xiǎo Wén hé tā māma yuànyi, wǒmen yě jiu bù néng shuō shénme le.

GRANDMA LǏ: Originally, Xiǎo Wén's father and I were both against it. After all, there's just no way that Chinese and Japanese can become part of the same family. But Xiǎo Wén and her mother wanted it, so there wasn't anything we could say about it.
TĀNGMǓ: Xiǎo Wén māma zěnme shuō ne?
TOM: What did Xiǎo Wén's mother say about it?
LǏ NǍINAI: Tā quànle wo hǎojǐcì. Tāde huà yǒu dàoli. Tā shuō, Zhōngguó rén hé Rìběn rén shi dǎguo zhàng. Kěshi xiànzài, shìqing yǐjīng guòqu jǐshínián le, wèishénme hái yào ràng háizimen chī kǔ ne?

GRANDMA LǏ: She tried to persuade me many times. What she said makes sense. She said that the Chinese and the Japanese did go to war, but now that it's all been over for a few decades, why should the children still be made to suffer for it?
TĀNGMǓ: Bómǔ shuōde duì. Èi, wǒ lái Xiānggǎng zènme duō tiān le, zěnme hái méi kànjian ta ne?
TOM: She's right about that. By the way, I've been here in Hong Kong for so many days now, how is it that I haven't seen him?
LǏ NǍINAI: Tā huí Rìběn kàn tā māma qu le, nèi shi ge xiàoshùnde háizi. Děng ni cóng dàlù huílaide shíhou, tā yě gāi huílai le.
GRANDMA LǏ: He went back to Japan to visit his mother. He's a very filial boy. He should be back by the time you come back from the mainland.
TĀNGMǓ: Zhēn yǒu yìsi!
TOM: That's so interesting!
LǏ NǍINAI: Yǒu yìsi ba, Tāngmǔ, nǐ bù zhīdao, rén lǎo le, guānniàn yě lǎo le, yǒude shíhour zhēnde yào gǎigai le.
GRANDMA LǏ: Oh, it's interesting all right. You don't know, Tom, when a person gets old, their ideas get old too. Sometimes one really has to change a bit.
LǏ PÍNG: Mā, nǐ huílai le?
LǏ PÍNG: Hi mom, you're back?
LǏ MĀMA: Huílai le.
LǏ PÍNG'S MOTHER: Hi, yeah, I'm back.
TĀNGMǓ: Bómǔ, wǒ shuō shénme hǎo ne? Nín shízài tài kèqi le.
TOM: Auntie, what can I say? This is really too polite of you.
LǏ MĀMA: Zhèidiǎn chīde, yòngde, dōu dàiqu, zhèi liǎngjiàn yīfu děng yíxia chuānchuan kàn, héshì bu héshì.
LǏ PÍNG'S MOTHER: This food and these things are for you to take with you. And these two things to wear you can try on later and see if they fit you.
TĀNGMǓ: Bómǔ, nà jiu xièxie le.
TOM: Well then, thanks a lot, auntie.
LǏ MĀMA: Nàme yìdiǎndiǎn dōngxi xiè shénme. Lùshang hǎohāo zhàogu zìjǐ, shìqing wánle jiù huílai, xiūxi jǐtiān zài huí Měiguó.

LǏ PÍNG'S MOTHER: Why should you thank me for these odds and ends! You just look after yourself very carefully while you're traveling, and when the job is finished come back here and rest up for a few days before you go back to America.
TĀNGMǓ: Èn, wǒ yídìng huílai.
TOM: Okay, I'll be sure and come back.

LǏ NǍINAI: Guò liǎngtiān, Xiǎo Píng, Xiǎo Wén yě yào zǒu le. Xiǎo Píng mā, jīnr wǎnshang zán dōu bú zuò fàn le. Děng huǐr Xiǎo Píng bàba huílai, yíkuàir chūqu chī wǎnfàn, gěi háizimen sòngsong xíng, hǎo bu hǎo?

GRANDMA LǏ: In another day or two Xiǎo Píng and Xiǎo Wén will be leaving too. Mom, let's not make dinner tonight. When Xiǎo Píng's father gets back, we'll all go out to dinner and have a going-away party for the kids, okay?
LǏ MĀMA: Hǎode, hǎode.
LǏ PÍNG'S MOTHER: All right.
